card.name: Small linking words in all-caps warnings
card.fires_on: Small linking words (the, with, in, that, which, it, if, although) inside warning text written in ALL CAPS, often about allergic reactions or blood effects of antibiotics.

modes.label: Linking words after a verb
modes.description: Prepositions or articles such as THE, WITH, IN following a verb like DISCONTINUE or OBSERVED in capitalized warnings.
modes.example: TO DRUGS. IF AN ALLERGIC REACTION TO CEFOTAXIME OCCURS, DISCONTINUE TREATMENT WITH<< THE>> DRUG. SERIOUS HYPERSENS

modes.label: Connectors starting a clause
modes.description: Relative words or conjunctions such as THAT, WHICH, IT, IF, ALTHOUGH that begin a new clause in all-caps text.
modes.example: THE EXTRAPYRAMIDAL SYMPTOMS<< WHICH>> CAN OCCUR SECONDARY TO PROMETH

card.writes: It pushes up all-caps function words such as OF, THE, AND, so the model continues in capitals.
card.plain: It fires on little connecting words in warning paragraphs printed entirely in capital letters.
